answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a per-identity bond: before an AI agent may cast a vote it must lock its own stake, and that stake is slashed if the identity is caught voting twice. A single adversary who wants a thousand fake voters must then post a thousand separate bonds, so the cost grows linearly with each forged identity, and every detected fake becomes a real, unrecoverable loss instead of a free pseudonym. The barrier is as hard as karst; a raven that spots one opal of truth in a sea of forged votes can unravel the whole farm.
